# NORTH STAR — LOCKED

**Effort:** Anchor Re-architecture — the Butler substrate
**Project:** C:\dev\Anchor · **Locked:** 2026-07-02 by John (as-is, via AskUserQuestion; FULL triage confirmed)
**Pipeline:** Crucible FULL (Stage 0 ✓ → Stage 1 → Stage 2 → Foreman)
**Drift rule:** drift detection is ACTIVE from this lock. Amendments only via the
documented North-Star-amendment path with John's approval.

---

## Objective

Re-architect Anchor from an 18,441-line monolith into a maintainable, observable,
restart-resilient substrate — the architectural foundation for the Butler (an always-on
agent that manages John's projects and workflow) — by (1) extracting the embedded
frontend to static files, (2) replacing the if-elif dispatch with a declarative
route table whose auth is default-deny by construction, (3) laying an append-only
per-project event-log spine (dual-write; legacy stores stay authoritative), and
(4) splitting spawned work into a supervisor process so the dashboard can restart
without killing in-flight jobs or terminals — all delivered incrementally, with the
dashboard fully working on :8777 at every merged step.

## Success criteria (measurable)

1. **Frontend extracted.** anchor_gui.py contains no embedded frontend blob larger than
   ~50 lines: `_PROJECT_WINDOW_JS` (5623–10285), the `generate_html` f-string JS/CSS
   (10966–13671), and the project-window HTML/CSS shell are served as static files via
   the existing traversal-safe asset-route idiom, with server state injected only
   through a small bootstrap JSON. Bar: behavior parity, Playwright-verified on the
   home dashboard and the project window; anchor_gui.py shrinks by ≥ 7,000 lines.
2. **One route table, declarative auth, default-deny.** All HTTP routes (~125 dispatch
   arms across do_GET/do_POST) dispatch through a single declarative table where EVERY
   route declares its auth policy; token is the default; unauthenticated routes exist
   only on an explicit, reviewed allowlist. The currently-unauthenticated GET data
   plane (/artifact, /report, /summary, /project, /api/rnd/projects, /api/rnd/tail,
   /api/rnd/jobs) is gated when ANCHOR_TOKEN is set, with browser page navigation still
   working (cookie or equivalent — no URL tokens except where WS demands it). Zero
   in-branch imports shadowing module names (the os/datetime class) remain.
3. **Event-log spine, dual-write, provably derivable.** Every mutation-of-record
   (session started/closed/killed/advanced, doc persisted, job launched/finished/
   cancelled, effort promoted, grass idea lifecycle, deliverable pinned/launched,
   project lifecycle, handoff recorded, boneyard capture) appends a schema-versioned
   event to an append-only per-project journal, written alongside — never instead of —
   the existing index/pointer/registry stores. A parity gate (in tests AND the daily
   healthcheck) re-derives the session/effort views from the journal and reports zero
   divergence; a recovery tool rebuilds a deleted index.json from the journal in a
   test. The "lost from an index" bug class becomes recoverable-by-construction.
4. **Supervisor split — restart survival, live-proven.** Spawned lane jobs are owned by
   a separate stdlib supervisor process (own NSSM service, loopback token-authed IPC,
   inline seam for tests/healthcheck): `nssm restart anchor` with a job in flight
   leaves the job running and the restarted dashboard reporting it live — demonstrated
   on the real service. PTY sessions follow behind a mandated ConPTY-across-processes
   spike; if the spike refutes economic feasibility, PTYs remain dashboard-owned and
   that narrowing is recorded honestly in the plan (jobs-half is non-negotiable).
5. **One markdown-parsing layer.** A single shared parsing module; anchor_gui.py and
   anchor.py import it (today's byte-identical twins de-forked); the drifted third copy
   dies with anchor_server.py, which is **deleted** (confirmed dead: Flask, port 5000,
   referenced by nothing).
6. **Runtime state out of the repo.** The live deployment runs with ANCHOR_DATA_DIR
   pointing outside C:\dev\Anchor (using the existing paths.py seam + migrate_data);
   `git status` on the repo is clean of runtime artifacts (~62 today) and stays clean
   through a healthcheck cycle.
7. **Never-broken increments.** Every merged step keeps the dashboard fully operational
   as the NSSM `anchor` service on :8777 (John's daily use never breaks); Python stdlib
   only (pywinpty exception stands); markdown files remain the source of truth for
   tasks; the full test suite stays green (modulo the 2–3 documented pre-existing
   flakes) and each pillar lands with its own test gate.

## Non-goals (explicit)

- **NOT building the Butler itself** — no autonomous scheduling/decision agent, no
  proactive actions; this effort delivers the substrate only.
- **NOT promoting the event log to source of truth** — no read-path cutover, no removal
  of index/pointer/registry stores; that is a later, separate effort.
- **NOT a UI redesign** — extraction is verbatim/behavior-parity; no visual or
  interaction changes beyond what parity requires.
- **NOT replacing markdown** as the task source of truth, and no new storage engines
  (no SQLite, no third-party deps).
- **NOT decomposing terminal_session.py** (Plan-1 Wave D item 13) — separate effort.
- **NOT changing John's ops surface** beyond adding the one supervisor service — the
  dashboard stays the NSSM `anchor` service on :8777.
- **NOT a big-bang rewrite** — any step that would leave the dashboard down or require
  a multi-day freeze is out.

## Constraints (inherited, binding)

Python stdlib only (pywinpty exception) · NSSM service `anchor` on :8777 · markdown
source of truth for tasks · incremental migration, dashboard working at every step ·
no visible console windows from spawned processes · sequenced after the
fix/review-wave-a-2026-07 merge to master (DONE — deployed 2026-07-02).

## Locked architectural decisions (Stage-0 D1–D3, John-approved with the lock)

- **D1:** per-project append-only JSONL journal, DUAL-WRITE (legacy stores stay
  authoritative for reads); parity gate + recovery tool are mandatory consumers.
- **D2:** separate stdlib supervisor as its own NSSM service, loopback token-authed
  IPC, inline seam for tests; JOBS first, PTYs behind the mandated ConPTY spike.
- **D3:** default-deny declarative route auth; `open` is an explicit reviewed
  allowlist; cookie-based browser navigation; strangler-style migration.

C2 One declarative route table, default-deny auth: all ~125 do_GET/do_POST dispatch arms route through a single table where EVERY route declares its auth policy (token default; open only on an explicit reviewed allowlist); the currently-unauthenticated GET data plane (/artifact, /report, /summary, /project, /api/rnd/projects, /api/rnd/tail, /api/rnd/jobs) is gated when ANCHOR_TOKEN is set, with browser page navigation still working via cookie (no URL tokens except where WS demands); zero in-branch imports shadowing module names remain.

summary: Seven phases toward the locked North Star, ordered by the cross-pillar dependency DAG (P0 rails → C1 extraction → C2 routes → C5/C6 hygiene → C3 journal → C4 supervisor → C7 closure), each merged wave revertible without reverting later waves via per-pillar off-switch flags (journal emission, auth warn/enforce, supervisor inline/external, static-vs-embedded frontend). Phase 0 front-loads every mechanical ground-truth gate (interpolation census, consumer enumeration, write-site tripwire, Playwright flows, contract-versioning shim, ConPTY spike with pre-written acceptance question and pre-designed drain fallback) so no later wave is sized or gated on hope. Every phase carries its own test gate plus the per-wave live-service smoke ritual (restart → GET / 200 → project window loads → on-demand healthcheck green), keeping the dashboard fully operational on :8777 at every merged step (C7). All 52 integrated ideas are absorbed; deferrals are named explicitly per phase — Butler behavior, journal read-path cutover, PTY supervisor ownership beyond the spike's verdict, and terminal_session.py decomposition remain out of scope per the North Star's non-goals.

phases.name: Phase 0 — Ground Truth & Safety Rails (pre-wave instrumentation)
phases.rationale: Serves C1, C2, C3, C4, and C7 by replacing hope with mechanical evidence before any wave is sized: the census sizes the extraction, the tripwire enumerates the true mutation set, the consumer inventory prevents auth lockouts, the spike verdict shapes supervisor sequencing, and the contract shim protects every later deploy. Nothing here changes runtime behavior, so C7 risk is near zero while every later phase's gate is manufactured here.
nearTermSpecifics: Write the interpolation-census script: mechanically classify EVERY {…} interpolation in generate_html and render_project_window_html as data/flag/markup-emitting with counts, and confirm _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS has zero; derive the actual shrink number from the census and gate Phase 1 on its output — if markup-emitting interpolations exceed a small threshold, amend the North-Star C1 bar to 'template + bootstrap JSON + small server-side include layer' NOW, not mid-wave (Integrated 1; Mitigation 1).

Build the one-time Playwright investment: scripted flows for the top-5 stateful behaviors — terminal open+type via stub PTY, pending-paste flush, drag-to-group, maximize/restore, v12 dock click — that run in the Phase-1 extraction gate and remain permanent regression assets for every later pillar (Integrated 5).

Run the consumer-enumeration pre-work: grep-driven inventory of every caller of every currently-open route (repo code, anchor_healthcheck.py's endpoint walk, .bat/.vbs launchers, scheduled tasks, personal scripts) and give each a token path FIRST — Authorization header accepted everywhere, ?token= retained only for WS/SSE (Integrated 13; Mitigation 4).

Build the write-site tripwire: a test-mode wrapper around file writes under .anchor/ that fails any test whose mutation did NOT append a journal event (journal allowlisted); run the full suite + healthcheck under it to enumerate the TRUE mutation-of-record set mechanically before designing Phase-3 instrumentation; it stays on forever as the C3 completeness gate (Integrated 20; Mitigation 5).

Ship the frontend↔backend contract-versioning shim in the LAST pre-migration release: ANCHOR_BOOT carries a build id, every _postJson sends it, the server answers a mismatch with a structured 409 the old client renders as a 'reload required' banner — so no later wave can strand a stale tab or PWA-cached iPad client (Integrated 8; Mitigation 12).

Insert sentinel-comment anchors in a tiny pre-wave commit and build the freshness gate that re-locates each structural anchor (the _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS assignment, the generate_html def, sentinels) and fails loudly on ambiguity before any EXECUTE — line numbers never appear in the implementation plan (Integrated 4; Mitigation 14).

Run the two spikes NOW, time-boxed, with acceptance questions written BEFORE they run: (a) ConPTY-across-processes — latency bound, re-attach behavior, complexity budget — so the answer shapes Phase-4 sequencing; (b) cookie-through-WS-upgrade on the REAL clients (desktop browser + iPhone PWA over Tailscale HTTPS), with ?token= declared as the WS fallback if the Cookie header doesn't survive (Integrated 14, 33; Mitigations 4, 10).

Pre-design the spike's 'no' branch fallback so it ships in the same wave as any narrowing: a graceful pre-restart drain in the deploy script — close_session park + capture_session_docs + W3 warm-resume seed for every live PTY (Integrated 34; Mitigation 10).

Write the three concrete Butler user stories ('what happened on project X this week', 'what did the user decide vs auto-advance', 'which job produced this doc') as the binding validation target for the Phase-3 event envelope (Integrated 23; Mitigation 13).

Draw the cross-pillar dependency DAG with revert-compatibility as a stated Stage-2 rule; define the four per-pillar off-switch flags (journal emission, auth warn/enforce, supervisor inline/external, static-vs-embedded frontend) and the named hybrid-state matrix with a healthcheck assertion of the CURRENT configuration (Integrated 42, 52; Mitigation 20).

Codify the standing rituals: per-wave live-service smoke in every merge checklist (nssm restart / drain script → GET / 200 → one project window loads → on-demand healthcheck green), the healthcheck SLO (wall-time cap, zero-known-flakes, each new walk runs 20× nightly before joining the 5AM run), and the sequencing rule that auth flips never ship in the same deploy as the JS calling the flipped routes (Integrated 43, 44, 45; Mitigation 15).
Declare the soft merge-freeze protocol on anchor_gui.py for the extraction wave specifically, coordinated with the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build's schedule (Integrated 9; Mitigation 14).
deferred: Any product-behavior change — Phase 0 is instrumentation, spikes, and process artifacts only.
Acting on the spike verdicts (Phase 4 consumes the ConPTY answer; Phase 2 consumes the cookie answer).
Journal module design details beyond the tripwire's mutation-set enumeration (Phase 3).

phases.name: Phase 1 — Frontend Extraction (C1)
phases.rationale: Serves C1 directly and de-risks everything after it: a ~7,000-line-smaller anchor_gui.py makes the Phase-2 route migration and Phase-5 parser extraction tractable, and the byte-parity gate makes this the safest big diff in the plan. Runs first because it is the one wave that cannot tolerate concurrent drift — the narrow merge-freeze happens once, here.
nearTermSpecifics: Land the extraction as THREE independently merged, byte-gated, live-smoked increments in dependency order: (1) _PROJECT_WINDOW_JS — raw string, census-confirmed zero interpolations, pure verbatim move; (2) the project-window HTML/CSS shell; (3) the generate_html f-string JS/CSS — the only genuinely fiddly one, sized and gated by the Phase-0 census (Integrated 50, 1).

Byte-parity golden-file gate: a build/test step renders via the OLD f-string path and the NEW static-file+bootstrap path and diffs the emitted JS/CSS byte-for-byte after {{/}} de-escaping; Playwright (home dashboard + project window + the top-5 flows) is reserved for the one thing that genuinely changed — the bootstrap-JSON seam (Integrated 2; Mitigation 2).

window.ANCHOR_BOOT as the ONLY server→client state channel: one small injected JSON object (token presence, project id, build id, feature flags, initial counts), documented as a versioned dict in one module; everything else in the extracted JS reads from it or existing API calls (Integrated 3).

Serve the static files through the EXISTING traversal-safe asset-route idiom (resolve()+relative_to, ValueError→None) already proven 4× in the repo — one new static root, zero new security surface (Integrated 6).

Content-hash cache-busting (?v=<hash8> minted at startup from file bytes) so a deploy always invalidates John's long-lived tabs — the documented stale-browser pitfall gains no static-file flavor (Integrated 7).
Soft merge-freeze on anchor_gui.py ACTIVE for this phase only, coordinated with the parked ship-Anchor-v1 build; the anchor-freshness gate re-runs before each increment's EXECUTE (Integrated 9, 4).
Keep the static-vs-embedded frontend off-switch flag functional through the phase so the wave is revertible without reverting anything after it (Integrated 42).
Exit gate: census-derived shrink number achieved (bar ≥7,000 lines unless the census forced the up-front amendment), byte-parity green, Playwright parity green, live smoke green.
deferred: Any UI redesign or interaction change — extraction is verbatim/behavior-parity per the North Star non-goal.
Refactoring the extracted JS (modules, bundling, linting) — the deliverable is the verbatim move; cleanup is a later, separate effort.
A server-side template/include layer BEYOND what the Phase-0 census forces via the up-front amendment path.

phases.name: Phase 2 — Declarative Route Table & Default-Deny Auth (C2)
phases.rationale: Serves C2. Runs after extraction so route handlers migrate out of a smaller file, and because the auth-flip sequencing rule requires the frontend to be stable and soaked before any route enforces. Strangler-style per D3: the table dispatches first, legacy if-elif chains catch the rest, and progress is a measurable count, not a narrative.
nearTermSpecifics: Build the route table where EVERY route — including streaming/upgrade specials — has a ROW (method, pattern, auth policy, handler kind: standard|stream|upgrade); the default-deny audit runs over rows; kind≠standard dispatch is honestly special-cased at the pre-dispatch hook with the row's auth check invoked FIRST. The auditable invariant is 'no route exists without a declared row' (Integrated 10; Mitigation 16).

Strangler dispatch with fallthrough: table first, unmatched falls through to the legacy chains; branches migrate in small reviewed batches; a coverage test counts remaining legacy arms so the audit knows exactly what the table does not yet govern (Integrated 16).

Handlers become module-level functions as they migrate — killing the os/datetime in-branch import-shadowing class as a free structural consequence; add a distro.py-style AST scan that fails on any in-method import shadowing a module-level name so the class can't return (Integrated 17).

OPEN_ROUTES as a checked-in reviewed artifact: a short table in the route module with a mandatory justification string per entry, plus a test asserting the live open set matches it exactly — any new open route requires editing the reviewed file (Integrated 18).

Explicit 401-before-101 socket-level regression test for term_ws: an unauthenticated upgrade attempt receives 401 before any handshake bytes, preserving the hand-rolled RFC-6455 ordering through the migration (Integrated 11).

ANCHOR_AUTH_WARN log-only mode: each route batch flips to 'warn' for a soak day on the live service (log who WOULD 401, allow through), the warn log is reviewed as a gate artifact, THEN 'enforce' — and never in the same deploy as JS that calls the flipped routes (Integrated 12, 45; Mitigation 4).
Apply the Phase-0 cookie-through-WS spike verdict: cookie-based browser navigation per D3, with ?token= retained only where the spike proved WS/SSE demands it (Integrated 14).

Ship /api/routes (token-authed) dumping the live table — path, method, auth policy, handler kind, legacy-or-migrated — and rewire the healthcheck's endpoint walk to iterate the declared rows (skipping kind=upgrade), asserting auth behavior per declared policy so an undeclared route can't hide from the daily check (Integrated 46, 51).

Ops-cutover gate with teeth: mint token → set NSSM AppEnvironmentExtra → restart → a healthcheck probe asserts the LIVE :8777 returns 401 on tokenless /api/rnd/projects. The phase is not DONE until that live assert passes; if John declines to run tokened, that is recorded as a North-Star amendment, never silently (Integrated 15; Mitigation 3).
deferred: Retiring the legacy if-elif chains entirely — migration continues in batches until the coverage counter hits zero; the phase gate is 'every route has a row + data plane enforced', not 'zero legacy arms' (the zero-arm milestone is tracked to completion within the effort but may trail the auth cutover).
Any auth model beyond token+cookie (no user accounts, no sessions-with-expiry, no TLS termination — Tailscale Serve HTTPS remains the transport answer from the anchor-as-app research).
Rate limiting, CSRF hardening, or audit logging of denied requests — Butler-era concerns.

phases.name: Phase 3 — Consolidation & Data Hygiene (C5 + C6)
phases.rationale: Serves C5 and C6. Sequenced here because both are independent of the journal/supervisor pillars, touch anchor_gui.py (so they follow the extraction and route phases rather than fighting them), and getting runtime state out of the repo BEFORE the journal lands means per-project journals are born outside the repo instead of migrated later.
nearTermSpecifics: Extract anchor_md.py: the byte-identical twin parsers (task/project/inbox/archived parsing in anchor_gui.py and anchor.py) become one shared module imported by both, with a golden-corpus gate — today's REAL markdown files parsed identically pre/post de-fork (Integrated 37).

Pre-deletion sweep for anchor_server.py: Get-ScheduledTask scan, Start-Menu/Desktop *.lnk target search for :5000/anchor_server, grep of _archive/ docs — then DELETE it (killing the drifted third parser copy) with a one-line tombstone in the changelog (Integrated 38; Mitigation 17).

Build the path-audit tool: scan every durable store (registry folder_path, worktree_path, discovery.json, job dirs, session records) for absolute paths under the repo root and emit a rewrite map (Integrated 39).

Execute the data-dir migration as ONE scripted, rollback-able unit: stop service → migrate_data (existing paths.py seam) → path-rewrite pass → start → healthcheck; old dir preserved read-only for a week (Integrated 39; Mitigation 11).

Boot-reaper dry-run for the first post-move boot: worktrees.reap_orphans runs report-only (ANCHOR_REAPER_DRYRUN) so a path-resolution miss can't cascade into deleted parked-session worktrees; re-armed only after a clean report (Integrated 40).

Git hygiene as its own separate commit + gate: git rm --cached the ~62 tracked runtime artifacts + .gitignore them, then a gate that runs a full healthcheck cycle and asserts `git status --porcelain` is empty — C6's 'stays clean' clause verified, not assumed (Integrated 41).

Exit gate: live service running with ANCHOR_DATA_DIR outside C:\dev\Anchor, healthcheck green from the relocated dir, repo clean through a full healthcheck cycle, anchor.py and anchor_gui.py both importing anchor_md, anchor_server.py gone.
deferred: De-duplication beyond the parsers (anchor_gui/anchor share other logic mirrors) — only the markdown-parsing layer is in C5's scope.
Any markdown format change — the format is the source of truth and stays byte-compatible.
Relocating the git repo itself or restructuring worktree layout beyond what the path-rewrite requires.

phases.name: Phase 4 — Event-Log Spine (C3)
phases.rationale: Serves C3 and lays the Butler's memory. Runs after the data-dir move so journals are born in the runtime data dir, and after the Phase-0 tripwire has mechanically enumerated the true mutation-of-record set so instrumentation is designed against evidence. Dual-write per D1 — legacy stores stay authoritative for reads.
nearTermSpecifics: journal.py with ONE emit() choke point: schema validation, monotonic per-project seq assignment, atomic append under WRITE_LOCK; a distro.py-style scan forbids json.dump/open-for-write to journal paths outside the module; blessed legacy-store wrappers are the only emit() call sites (Integrated 19).

Butler-shaped envelope, reserve-and-ignore: mandatory correlation_id, causation_id, actor{kind,id} (user-click | auto-advance | healthcheck-synthetic | cli), per-project seq + wall ts, schema_ver — validated against the three Phase-0 Butler user stories, answerable from envelope fields alone; schema-evolution rule (additive-only within a major ver, unknown-field-tolerant readers) as a binding convention in the module docstring, with a v1-through-v-current round-trip test (Integrated 23, 24; Mitigation 13).

Journal-first write order by decree: emit the event, THEN write the legacy store — an orphaned journal event is a benign 'intent' record; 'journal-ahead' documented as expected crash residue with an idempotent replay path (Integrated 21; Mitigation 6).

Instrument the mutation-of-record set the tripwire enumerated (the C3 list: session lifecycle, doc persisted, job lifecycle, effort promoted, grass lifecycle, deliverable pinned/launched, project lifecycle, handoff, boneyard); per-tick/telemetry writes excluded BY RULE; the tripwire stays on permanently as the completeness gate (Integrated 20, 26).

Quiescent, classifying parity gate in tests AND the daily healthcheck: derive session/effort views from a WRITE_LOCK-bracketed snapshot copy, tolerate a bounded tail window of recent events, classify divergence (journal-ahead=OK/crash-residue, legacy-ahead=BUG, conflict=BUG); reconcile-report tool ships alongside (Integrated 22; Mitigation 6).

rebuild_index.py as a first-class deliverable: re-derives a deleted/torn index.json (and sessions.json rows) from the journal, proven by a test that deletes the index mid-suite, plus a documented operator runbook — the 'lost from an index' class becomes recoverable-by-construction (Integrated 25).

Idempotent event-replay tool: re-applying the journal against the legacy stores converges them (bounded, dry-run-first) — the operational answer to a legacy-ahead or conflict classification (Integrated 48).

`anchor.py rnd events <pid> [--since seq]` journal-tail CLI following the established v3–v12 CLI-mirror convention — immediately useful for debugging dual-write, the first taste of the journal as a queryable record (Integrated 47).

Perf budget gate: time the healthcheck's v2–v5 walks journal-on vs journal-off with a hard <5% regression budget; one appender per project, O(1) open-append-close, fsync policy configurable (Integrated 26; Mitigation 19).
The journal-emission off-switch flag stays functional; the parity walk runs 20× nightly before joining the 5AM run per the Phase-0 SLO discipline (Integrated 42, 43).
deferred: Read-path cutover / journal as source of truth — explicitly a later, separate effort per the North Star non-goal.
Journal retention, compaction, or cross-project aggregation — the Butler effort decides those against real query patterns.
Any Butler query surface beyond the events CLI and /api/routes-style introspection — the three user stories validate the schema; building the answers is Butler work.

phases.name: Phase 5 — Supervisor Split (C4)
phases.rationale: Serves C4, the restart-survival keystone. Runs last among the pillars because it deploys a second NSSM service (the one ops-surface change), consumes the Phase-0 ConPTY spike verdict, and benefits from the journal (durable job records) and route table (IPC-adjacent auth) already being in place. Jobs first per D2; PTYs strictly behind the spike's answer.
nearTermSpecifics: Write the IPC contract table as a Stage-2 artifact BEFORE code: every dashboard↔job interaction (launch, tail-since, cancel, gate-answer, cost/rollup, swarm-register) gets a row with state owner, idempotency key, and defined behavior when EITHER side restarts mid-interaction — including the tail-cursor-durability row (supervisor persists per-job read offsets in the job dir so /api/rnd/tail cursors survive a supervisor restart) (Integrated 27, 49; Mitigation 7).

ANCHOR_SUPERVISOR=inline|external seam from day one: the supervisor API is a Python interface with two implementations — in-process (tests, healthcheck, degraded mode) and loopback token-authed HTTP client (production) — so the 4,970-line healthcheck and the suite never need a second real process, and 'supervisor down' has a defined degraded behavior (Integrated 35).

In-memory-structure rebuild table in the implementation plan: every dashboard-side structure (_LIVE, _JOB_DIRS, _ACTIVE_LANE, _FOLDER_BUILD, lane locks, SSE attach points) gets a rebuild-source column (durable record | supervisor query); any row with no rebuild source is a named design hole resolved before EXECUTE (Integrated 30; Mitigation 8).

Gate-answer durability: an AskUserQuestion answer is durably queued in the supervisor (persisted to the job dir) and ACKed before the dashboard POST returns; the stdin write happens supervisor-side against the handle it owns — a dropped IPC hop is retryable, never lost (Integrated 28).

The LITERAL automated gate: a stub-seam test matrix that (a) kills each side mid-interaction per contract-table row, and (b) restarts the dashboard side with a job in flight and asserts the restarted dashboard lists the SAME job_id as running, serves an advancing tail cursor, and can cancel it (Integrated 29; Mitigations 7, 8).

install_supervisor.ps1 — scripted, not documented: nssm install + ObjectName .\john + AppEnvironmentExtra cloned from the anchor service + CREATE_NO_WINDOW discipline, because claude.exe credentials live in John's profile and no spawned process may pop a console (Integrated 31).

Two live healthcheck probes the inline seam can never cover: (a) ask the LIVE supervisor to spawn a trivial claude.exe --version child and report output (credentials + PATH proven under the real service account); (b) restart the SUPERVISOR with a sacrificial child running and assert the child survived (job-object breakaway proven) (Integrated 32).

C4 live demo as a runbook artifact executed WITH John: dedicated throwaway R&D project on the real service, a harmless long-running real job through the REAL launch path (fake_claude-driven), exact elevated commands, expected observations, rollback steps (supervisor stop + lane-lock clear); the criterion is honestly unmet until the runbook has run once (Integrated 36; Mitigation 18).

Apply the ConPTY spike verdict: if YES, schedule PTY adoption as a follow-on wave inside this phase's plan; if NO, ship the pre-designed graceful pre-restart drain (close_session park + capture_session_docs + warm-resume seed for every live PTY, automated in the deploy script) in the SAME wave as the honestly-recorded narrowing — so every remaining deploy of this effort costs a warm reconnect, not dead context (Integrated 33, 34; Mitigation 10).
deferred: PTY sessions moving to the supervisor when the spike refutes economic feasibility — recorded as an honest North-Star-sanctioned narrowing, revisitable as its own effort (the jobs half is non-negotiable and ships regardless).
Supervisor ownership of preview servers, background summarizers, or the healthcheck itself — jobs only in this effort.
Multi-host or remote supervisor (Tailscale-reachable job host) — Butler-era.
Supervisor-side scheduling/queueing policy beyond what job_runner already does — the split moves ownership, it does not redesign job semantics.

phases.name: Phase 6 — Closure: Hybrid-State Hardening & North-Star Scorecard (C7)
phases.rationale: Serves C7 and closes the effort honestly: the four pillar flags now span a real configuration space, the healthcheck carries four new walks, and every criterion needs a demonstrated (not narrated) verdict. This phase converts 'we built it' into 'the daily 5AM run and the live service prove it, continuously'.
nearTermSpecifics: Finalize the named hybrid-state matrix: each supported combination of the four pillar flags gets a one-line support statement, and the healthcheck asserts the CURRENT live configuration is a named state (Integrated 52).

Wire the four new healthcheck walks (journal parity gate, supervisor probes, cookie/auth walk, relocated-data-dir walk) into the 5AM run ONLY after each has run 20× in nightly repetition under the SLO (wall-time cap, zero-known-flakes, quiescence strategy, retry-with-classification, 'Auto-fixes applied' degradation path) (Integrated 43).

Run the final live sign-offs in one sitting with John: the C4 restart-survival runbook, the C2 tokenless-401 live assert, a C6 healthcheck-cycle-then-clean-git-status check, and the per-wave smoke on the final merged state (Integrated 15, 36, 41, 44).

Emit the North-Star scorecard: each of C1–C7 marked met/narrowed/unmet with the gate artifact that proves it (census+byte-diff for C1, OPEN_ROUTES+live 401 for C2, parity gate+rebuild test for C3, runbook execution for C4, golden-corpus+tombstone for C5, clean-porcelain gate for C6, green suite+smoke log for C7); any narrowing (PTY spike 'no', John declining tokened ops) recorded via the documented amendment path, never silently.

Retire the temporary scaffolding honestly: the strangler fallthrough's remaining-legacy-arms counter driven to zero or its residual explicitly carried as named debt; the extraction-wave merge-freeze formally lifted; the old data dir's read-only week concluded and the dir archived.
deferred: Building the Butler itself — the substrate is done; the always-on agent, its scheduling, and its proactive actions are the next locked effort.
Promoting the journal to read-path source of truth — separate effort, now provably possible via the parity gate.
terminal_session.py decomposition (Plan-1 Wave D item 13) — separate effort per the North Star non-goal.
Removing the pillar off-switch flags — they stay as supported operational levers until the Butler effort decides otherwise.
